meta.description: Hybrid pipeline specifications for tasks T04 and T07. Each pipeline runs a deterministic regex stage first; only unmatched inputs proceed to the LLM stage.
meta.expected_aggregate_llm_call_rate_note: Weighted average across T04 and T07. Without this hybrid layer, both tasks would route 100% to LLM.

step_1_regex.description: Try to extract a full name using common introductory phrase patterns.

patterns.note: Handles 'My name is Sarah Johnson' and 'My name's Tom Smith'. IGNORECASE because customers sometimes type lowercase.
patterns.example_match: My name is Sarah Johnson and I'm having trouble logging in.

patterns.note: Handles 'This is Marcus Rivera', 'I'm Priya Nair', 'It's Tom Bruckner'. IGNORECASE applied.
patterns.example_match: Hi, this is Marcus Rivera. I'd like to update my billing address.

patterns.note: Catches trailing phrasings: 'The name is Dana Cho', '...name is Dana Cho'.
patterns.example_match: 4421983 — that's my account. The name is Dana Cho.

step_2_sanity_check.description: Before accepting the regex result, run a lightweight sanity check.
checks: Captured string contains exactly one space (first + last name; reject if title/suffix complicates it)
Each word starts with an uppercase letter after .title() normalization
Neither word is in a blocklist of common non-name words: ['This', 'That', 'The', 'Your', 'My']

step_3_llm_fallback.description: Call claude-haiku-4-5 only when regex produced no match or sanity check failed.
step_3_llm_fallback.prompt_template:
Extract the customer's full name from the following support message. Return only the name (first and last) with no explanation. If no name is present, return null.

Message: {message}

regex_should_handle.input: My name is Sarah Johnson and I'm having trouble logging in.
Hi, this is Marcus Rivera. I'd like to update my billing address.
I'm Priya Nair. My account number is ACC-4481923.
4421983 — that's my account. The name is Dana Cho.

llm_should_handle.input: Hey — it's Tom. Tom Bruckner. I placed an order last week.

llm_should_handle.note: Lowercase, single name, no intro phrase

llm_should_handle.input: This is the third time I've called about this.
llm_should_handle.note: 'This is' pattern fires but no name follows — sanity check blocks

step_1_regex.description: Extract formal product codes in the format PROD-XX000 (two uppercase letters + three digits).
step_1_regex.python_implementation:
import re

_PRODUCT_CODE_PATTERN = re.compile(r'PROD-[A-Z]{2}\d{3}')

def extract_product_codes_regex(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """
    Returns all formal product codes found in the text.
    Returns empty list (not None) to distinguish 'no codes found' from error.
    """
    return _PRODUCT_CODE_PATTERN.findall(text)
step_1_regex.example_match: The PROD-PR001 plan and the PROD-AD005 add-on are both broken.

step_2_llm_enrichment.description: After extracting formal codes, always call LLM to capture free-form product mentions the regex cannot handle. The LLM result is merged with the regex result (union, deduplicated).
step_2_llm_enrichment.rationale: Unlike T04 where LLM is a pure fallback, here LLM runs on every message because free-form product names (60% of mentions) provide business-critical information. The regex reduces LLM workload by pre-annotating formal codes so the LLM does not need to extract them again.
step_2_llm_enrichment.note: LLM is called only when regex found no codes OR always — see step_2_always_llm flag below
step_2_llm_enrichment.always_llm_rationale: LLM is called only when regex extracts zero codes. If formal codes were found, we skip the LLM enrichment call unless the message is longer than 120 characters (indicating free-form text is likely present alongside the code).

step_3_merge.description: Merge regex codes and LLM-extracted names into a single deduplicated list.

regex_captures_fully.input: The PROD-PR001 plan and the PROD-AD005 add-on are both broken.
regex_captures_fully.note: Short message, codes found, LLM skipped

monitoring.promote_threshold_note: T07 is unlikely to promote to full regex given the open-vocabulary nature of product mentions; monitor for code-format adoption instead

economic_summary.note: Hybrid savings are modest at 5K/day volume but the pattern is correct regardless of scale. At 100K daily parses the monthly saving is ~$31.20.
